corrections.why: The record's position (from OSM) is that of the eastern tower; the western tower stands about 300 yards west, at the coordinates Lighthousefriends gives for the west tower.
The western light was discontinued in 1924; only the eastern tower remains an aid to navigation.
The 1828 towers were rubblestone and were replaced by cast-iron towers in 1874; the 1828 date belongs to the station, not the standing tower.
The characteristic belongs to the eastern tower's light; the western tower no longer shows a light.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The western light was discontinued in 1924; the eastern tower is the one still lit.

notes_for_editor: Built mainly from the NRHP nomination, D'Entremont and Lighthousefriends (both modern, copyrighted; paraphrased), 1882 Portland Daily Press pages, two Light-House Board reports (1893, 1901) and the 1932 Bulletin. No source found that sorts keepers by tower; the roster lists only people a source ties to the western light (Staples family from D'Entremont; Ira Winn from USLHS). Disagreements flagged in the text: Merrill's purchase (NRHP 1959 reading vs D'Entremont/others 1971), discontinuance year (1882 decision in the Press vs 1883 per Lighthousefriends), tower height 65 vs 67 ft, distance between towers (895 ft for 1828 towers; 923 ft Lighthousefriends vs 300 yd NRHP for 1874), 1893 report says the second assistant tended the southwest tower while Lighthousefriends puts the first assistant's dwelling there in 1878. The date the west light was relit after 1882 was not found (Chronicling America pages for Jan 1883 timed out). The 1893 Board report passage is OCR; the volume page (scan 56) printed number not confirmed. Lighthousefriends also says the west tower got a third-order fixed lens from Matinicus Rock in 1924; not used. Staples dates 1861-1865 are approximate (Civil War; Michael Staples 1861-1869 on USLHS roster); Asbury is not on the USLHS roster. The USLHS west-tower page lists only a contractor. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Staples roster dates removed (D'Entremont gives only c. 1860s); 1893 report passage confirmed at scan 56 (1893 report; printed p.47 unconfirmed).
